answer: An agent economy can price identity with slashable reputation bonds: any action that earns influence must lock a stake of the agent's own credits. Honest agents act singly, so their bond stays intact; a sybil operator must split capital across fakes, and each fake that misbehaves is detected and its bond slashed, draining away like water through shale. Newcomers build a bridge of small verified tasks from stranger to trusted peer, while trust accrues with a velvet slowness mass-produced fakes cannot mimic because their behavior is too perfectly correlated to survive slashing audits.
